\chapter{Chapter03 — Estimator}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.GoldreichLevin.Estimator}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier observation work]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, a set of coordinates $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and a
subset $S\subseteq J$, the observation work is $2n+2|S|+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier observation program]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, let $S\subseteq J$, and
choose a sign assignment $z$ outside $J$ and sign assignments $y,y'$ on $J$. The
membership-query program queries the target at the two full sign vectors obtained by
combining $y,z$ and $y',z$, respectively; after receiving answers $a,a'\in\{−1,1\}$, it
charges $2n+2|S|+1$ local computation steps and returns the rational restricted Fourier
weight observation determined by $J,S,z,y,y',a,a'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Continuation for batched Fourier observations]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ and $S\subseteq J$, and let
$m\in\mathbb N$. Given three lists of $m$ sign vectors, a list of rational observations,
and a continuation that takes a list of rational observations to a membership-query
program with output type $\beta$, this program processes the vectors in order. At each
position it takes the coordinates outside $J$ from the first vector and the coordinates
on $J$ from the second and third vectors, queries the target at the two resulting
combined vectors, charges $2n+2|S|+1$ local steps, and adds the resulting rational
restricted Fourier weight observation; after all $m$ positions it passes the
observations in their original order to the continuation.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Batched restricted Fourier observation program]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, let $S\subseteq J$, and
let $m\in\mathbb N$. Given three lists of $m$ sign vectors, the membership-query program
processes them position by position as follows: it uses the first vector's coordinates
outside $J$ and the second and third vectors' coordinates on $J$ to form two inputs,
queries the target at both, and records the resulting rational restricted Fourier weight
observation, charging $2n+2|S|+1$ local steps for each position. It returns the list of
the $m$ observations in their original order.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Batched Fourier observation output]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, let $S\subseteq J$, and let $m\in\mathbb N$. For each of
three lists of $m$ sign vectors, form at each position two inputs using the first
vector's coordinates outside $J$ and the second and third vectors' coordinates on $J$.
The output is the length-$m$ list, in the original order, of the rational restricted
Fourier weight observations obtained from these two inputs and their values under $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Batched Fourier observation output]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, let $S\subseteq J$, and let $m\in\mathbb N$. Given three
lists of $m$ sign vectors, the output is the length-$m$ list, in their original order,
of rational restricted Fourier weight observations: at each position, use the first
vector's coordinates outside $J$ and the second and third vectors' coordinates on $J$ to
form two inputs, and evaluate $f$ at both.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Batch output as an appended list]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux_eq_append_ofFn}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux_eq_append_ofFn}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $S\subseteq J$, let $O$ be a list of rational
numbers, and let $z_i,y_i,y'_i$ be three cube inputs for each $i<m$. The batch output
auxiliary procedure, started with $O$, returns the reverse of $O$ followed by the list,
in index order, of the rational restricted Fourier weight observations formed from
$z_i,y_i,y'_i$ and the labels supplied by $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Batch of restricted Fourier observations]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput_eq_ofFn}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput_eq_ofFn}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux_eq_append_ofFn}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $J$ be a set of coordinates in $\bbr^n$, let $S$ be a
finite subset of $J$, and let a Boolean target function and three length-$m$ sequences
of sign-cube inputs be given. The batch output is the length-$m$ list whose $i$th entry
is the rational restricted Fourier weight observation formed from the fixed-coordinate
part of the $i$th input in the first sequence, the free-coordinate parts of the $i$th
inputs in the second and third sequences, and the target values at the resulting
combined inputs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Empirical restricted Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.empiricalRestrictedFourierWeight}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002
}
\label{FABL.empiricalRestrictedFourierWeight}
\leanok
For a natural number $m$ and a finite list of rational observations, the empirical
restricted Fourier weight is the sum of the observations divided by $m$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier weight estimator program]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.empiricalRestrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, let $S\subseteq J$, and
let $m\in\mathbb N$. The membership-query program draws three batches of $m$ uniform
sign vectors, then, position by position, uses the first batch's coordinates outside $J$
and the second and third batches' coordinates on $J$ to form two inputs and queries the
target at both. It records the rational restricted Fourier weight observations, charges
$2n+2|S|+1$ local steps per position and a further $m+1$ steps, and returns their sum
divided by $m$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Scheduled restricted Fourier estimator]
\lean{FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003}
\label{FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, let $S\subseteq J$, and
let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq\tfrac12$ and
$0<\delta\leq\tfrac12$. The scheduled estimator is the membership-query program for
estimating the restricted Fourier weight using the sample count prescribed by
$\varepsilon$ and $\delta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier estimator cost]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
For a finite coordinate set $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, a subset $S\subseteq J$, and a
sample size $m\in\mathbb{N}$, the estimator cost has $0$ random-example calls, $2m$
membership queries, and $3mn+m(2+w(J,S))+(m+1)$ units of work, where $w(J,S)$ is the
restricted Fourier weight observation work.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restricted Fourier estimator output]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003
}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.empiricalRestrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
and $S\subseteq J$ be finite, and let $m\in\mathbb{N}$. Given three $m$-tuples of
Boolean inputs $z,y,y'$, the output is the empirical restricted Fourier weight of the
observation batch formed from $f,J,S$ and those inputs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real restricted Fourier estimator output]
\lean{FABL.realRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p158-b003}
\label{FABL.realRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
and $S\subseteq J$ be finite, and let $m\in\mathbb{N}$. Given three $m$-tuples of
Boolean inputs $z,y,y'$, the real output is the sum of the corresponding restricted
Fourier weight observations divided by $m$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator output as an average]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput_eq_sum}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.empiricalRestrictedFourierWeight, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput_eq_ofFn}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and let $S\subseteq J$. Given three lists of $m$ cube
inputs, the rational restricted Fourier weight estimator output equals
$\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} r_i$, where $r_i$ is the rational restricted Fourier weight
observation formed from the $i$th inputs in the three lists and the labels supplied by
$f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real form of the estimator output]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput_cast}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservationFromInputs_cast, FABL.realRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput_eq_sum}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and let $S\subseteq J$. Given three lists of $m$ cube
inputs, the rational restricted Fourier weight estimator output, viewed as a real
number, equals the sum of the corresponding real restricted Fourier weight observations
divided by $m$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J$ be a set of coordinate indices, let $S\subseteq J$,
and let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Let $m$
be a positive integer and let $\varepsilon\ge0$. Draw three independent batches, each
consisting of $m$ independent uniform points from the sign cube, and compute the real
restricted Fourier weight estimator for $f$, $J$, and $S$. The probability that its
absolute error from the restricted Fourier weight exceeds or equals $\varepsilon$ is at
most $2\exp(-m\varepsilon^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Batch cost for restricted Fourier weight observations]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchCost}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $S$ be a subset of $J$, and
let $m\in\mathbb N$. The batch cost is the triple consisting of zero random-example
oracle calls, $2m$ membership queries, and $m$ times $2$ plus the
restricted-Fourier-weight observation work for $J$ and $S$ local computation steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Cost of one restricted Fourier observation]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.rationalRestrictedFourierWeightObservation, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationProgram, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J$ be a finite subset of $	ext{Fin}(n)$, let $S$ be a
finite subset of $J$, and let $z$ be a sign assignment on the coordinates outside $J$,
while $y,y'$ are sign assignments on $J$. For any Boolean target on the sign cube,
running the program that queries the target at the two cube points formed from $(y,z)$
and $(y',z)$ and returns the product of their restricted Fourier observations has the
deterministic output equal to that product, evaluated using the two target answers, and
cost $(0,2,2+2n+2|S|+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cost of a batch observation program]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith_pure}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith_pure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $J$ be a finite subset of the coordinates
$	ext{Fin}(n)$, and let $S$ be a finite subset of $J$. For a Boolean target on the sign
cube, three prescribed sequences of $m$ cube inputs, and an initial list of rational
observations, running the batch program that pairs the fixed-coordinate part of each
first input with the free-coordinate parts of the other two, queries the target at both
resulting inputs, records the product of their restricted Fourier observations, and
charges the prescribed local work has a deterministic output list given by those
observations together with the initial list, in its specified order; its cost is
$(0,2m,m(2+2n+2|S|+1))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restricted Fourier observation batch run]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutput, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgram, FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith_pure}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $S\subseteq J$,
let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and fix three sequences $z,y,y'\in(\{−1,1\}^n)^m$. The
observation batch program returns its list of restricted Fourier observations for these
inputs and target with probability one, at cost $\bigl(0,2m,m(2+2n+2|S|+1)\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empirical restricted Fourier estimate run]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith_empirical}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith_empirical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.empiricalRestrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchOutputAux, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationBatchProgramWith, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightObservationWork}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$, $m$, and $q$ be natural numbers, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let
$S\subseteq J$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, fix three sequences
$z,y,y'\in(\{−1,1\}^n)^m$, and fix a list $O$ of rational observations. The observation
program followed by the specified finishing step returns the empirical restricted
Fourier weight with denominator $q$, computed from the list obtained by appending the
observations generated by the batch program to $O$, with probability one. Its cost is
$\bigl(0,2m,m(2+2n+2|S|+1)+(q+1)\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restricted Fourier estimator run distribution]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_uniformProduct}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_uniformProduct}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorOutput, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram, FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformPMF_bind_bind_map_triple}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $S\subseteq J$,
and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$. The estimator’s run law is that of drawing three
independent uniformly random sequences $z,y,y'\in(\{−1,1\}^n)^m$ and returning its
restricted Fourier weight estimate computed from these sequences and $f$. Every outcome
has the estimator’s specified cost $\bigl(0,2m,3mn+m(2+2n+2|S|+1)+(m+1)\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator program cost]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_cost_eq}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_cost_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram, FABL.runWithCost_restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and let $S\subseteq J$. Every outcome $(q,c)$ in the
support of the estimator program's cost distribution for target $f$ has cost component
$c$ equal to the restricted Fourier weight estimator cost: zero random examples, $2m$
membership queries, and $3mn+m(2+(2n+2|S|+1))+(m+1)$ units of local work.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scheduled restricted estimator query count]
\lean{FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_queries_eq}
\label{FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_queries_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_cost_eq, FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube, let
$J$ be a subset of the coordinates, and let $S$ be a subset of $J$. For rational
parameters $\varepsilon,\delta$ with $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$, every outcome in the
support of the scheduled restricted Fourier weight estimator's cost distribution has
query count $2m$, where $m=\lceil2b(\delta)/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ and
$b(\delta)=\lceil\log_2\lceil2/\delta\rceil\rceil$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator work formula]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost_work}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost_work}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates,
and let $S\subseteq J$. The work component of the restricted Fourier weight estimator
cost is $3mn+m(2+(2n+2|S|+1))+(m+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator work bound]
\lean{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost_work_le}
\label{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost_work_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost_work}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $J$ be a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates,
and let $S\subseteq J$. The work component of the restricted Fourier weight estimator
cost is at most $8(m+1)(n+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Failure-bit count from a real parameter]
\lean{FABL.realRestrictedFourierWeightFailureBits}
\label{FABL.realRestrictedFourierWeightFailureBits}
\leanok
For $\delta\in\mathbb R$, define the failure-bit count to be
$\left\lceil\log_2\!\left(\left\lceil\frac{4}{\min(\delta,1/2)}\right\rceil\right)\right\rceil$,
where the inner and outer ceilings are taken as indicated by the natural-number ceiling
and base-$2$ logarithm ceiling.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison of failure-bit counts]
\lean{FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits_le_realRestrictedFourierWeightFailureBits}
\label{FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits_le_realRestrictedFourierWeightFailureBits}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.realRestrictedFourierWeightFailureBits}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\delta'$ be rational with $0<\delta'\leq 1/2$, and let $\delta>0$ be real. If
$\min(\delta,1/2)/2<\delta'$, then the failure-bit count $\lceil\log_2\lceil
2/\delta'\rceil\rceil$ is at most the real restricted Fourier-weight failure-bit count
$\lceil\log_2\lceil 4/\min(\delta,1/2)\rceil\rceil$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_failureProbability_le}
  {direct}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and
let $S\subseteq J$. Write $W_f(J,S)$ for the restricted Fourier weight: the sum of
squared Fourier coefficients at frequencies formed by adjoining to $S$ any subset of
coordinates outside $J$. For real $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, there are rationals
$\varepsilon',\delta'\in(0,\tfrac12]$, each strictly between half of the minimum of its
corresponding parameter and $\tfrac12$, such that the scheduled estimator with
parameters $\varepsilon',\delta'$ has probability at most $\delta$ of returning an
estimate whose absolute error in estimating $W_f(J,S)$ is at least $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Estimator accuracy and resource bounds]
\lean{FABL.exists_scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_with_resource_bounds}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005
}
\label{FABL.exists_scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_with_resource_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.LearningProgram.eventProbability, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.exists_scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_failureProbability_le, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits, FABL.fourierEstimatorFailureBits_le_realRestrictedFourierWeightFailureBits, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount_cast_le, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount_pos, FABL.realRestrictedFourierWeightFailureBits, FABL.restrictedFourierWeight, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorCost_work_le, FABL.restrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_cost_eq, FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram, FABL.scheduledRestrictedFourierWeightEstimatorProgram_queries_eq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $S\subseteq J$, and
write $W_f(J,S)$ for the sum of squared Fourier coefficients at frequencies formed by
adjoining to $S$ any subset of coordinates outside $J$. For real $\varepsilon,\delta>0$,
there are rationals $\varepsilon',\delta'\in(0,\tfrac12]$, each strictly between half of
the minimum of its corresponding parameter and $\tfrac12$, such that the scheduled
estimator with parameters $\varepsilon',\delta'$ has probability at most $\delta$ of
error at least $\varepsilon$. Moreover, writing
$F=\lceil\log_2\lceil4/\min\{\delta,\tfrac12\}\rceil\rceil$, its failure-bit count is at
most $F$, its sample count is at most $16F/\min\{\varepsilon,\tfrac12\}^2$, and every
outcome in the support has query cost at most $32F/\min\{\varepsilon,\tfrac12\}^2$ and
work cost at most $256F(n+1)/\min\{\varepsilon,\tfrac12\}^2$.
\end{theorem}
